nrel_summary: The maximum height for all ground-mounted systems is 20 feet when the system is oriented at maximum tilt. For farms in the Agricultural and Low Density Residential Zones that utilize agrivoltaic farming, the Planning Board may approve a greater height if it finds a greater height is necessary to accommodate continued or new agricultural activity. This applies to large-scale ground-mounted photovoltaic systems as defined by a footprint greater than 7,000 square feet up to a maximum of 35 acres. The height limit is explicitly stated in subsection F(1) and applies to all ground-mounted photovoltaic systems, including large-scale systems.

Large-scale ground-mounted photovoltaic systems have a total solar facility footprint greater than 7,000 square feet up to a maximum of 35 acres. Other size categories include small-scale systems (2,000 square feet or less) and medium-scale systems (more than 2,000 square feet up to and including 7,000 square feet). The maximum size for large-scale systems is explicitly stated as 35 acres.

For large-scale ground-mounted photovoltaic solar energy systems (defined as having a total solar facility footprint greater than 7,000 square feet up to a maximum of 35 acres), the setback measured from the lot line to the closest part of the photovoltaic solar energy system is a seventy-five feet minimum from all lot lines. Roads, landscaping and fencing may occur within the setback. The Planning Board may consider a solar facility project that is comprised of several lots to be treated as a single lot for purposes of applying setback standards. Other setback options for smaller systems include: small-scale systems require ten feet minimum from side and rear yard lot lines and a front lot line setback equal to the maximum required front yard in the zone (or 50 feet in certain zones); medium-scale systems require sixty feet minimum from lot lines abutting non-commercial/industrial zones, thirty feet minimum from lot lines abutting commercial/industrial zones, and front lot line setbacks similar to small-scale but with some zone exceptions.

The maximum Total Height of any WECS shall be 410 feet. 'Total Height' is defined as the height of the tower and the furthest vertical extension of the WECS. This applies to all Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS), which are machines converting wind kinetic energy into usable energy, commonly known as wind turbines.

section: §15 Setbacks and Noise Standards for Wind Energy Conversion Systems
nrel_summary: The Sound Level statistical sound pressure level (L10) shall not exceed the Ambient Sound Level by more than 6 dBA at the nearest property line to any proposed WECS. If the Ambient Sound Level exceeds 50 dBA, the standard shall be the Ambient Sound Level plus a maximum of 5 dBA. Independent certification shall be provided before and after construction demonstrating compliance with this requirement.

section: §15 Setbacks and Noise Standards for Wind Energy Conversion Systems
nrel_summary: Each WECS shall be setback from Site boundaries, measured from the center of the applicable component part of the WECS: Twelve hundred (1,200) feet from the nearest Site boundary property line. One and a half times the Total Height of the WECS from any non-residential structure (other than a school or church) or any above-ground utilities, unless waived by the utility companies.

section: §15 Setbacks and Noise Standards for Wind Energy Conversion Systems
nrel_summary: The ordinance requires a setback of two thousand (2,000) feet from the nearest off-site residence, measured from the exterior of such residence, for any tower, turbine, windmill, building housing mechanical components or electrical substation that is part of any Wind Energy Conversion System or Facility, unless specifically waived or varied by the Planning Board as part of a permit.

Commercial Solar Energy System: IUP (Allowed as interim use) in Agriculture (AG1/AG2/AG4), Rural Residential (RR5/RR10/RR20), Commercial, and Industrial districts; N (Not permitted) in Rural Townsite (RT0.5/RT1/RT2.5). Non-commercial Solar and Wind Energy Systems are permitted (P) in all listed districts.

The required setback from neighboring property lines for all project elements including structures, panels, racking systems, but excluding security enclosure, is 50 feet from all non-right-of-way property lines or 275 feet from any dwelling whichever is greater. The minimum setback from public roads shall be 100 feet from centerline.

section: Chapter 7020, as amended. Commercial Solar Energy Production Setbacks
nrel_summary: The required setback from any dwelling is 275 feet or 50 feet from neighboring property lines, whichever is greater, for all project elements including structures, panels, racking systems, but excluding security enclosure. Other setback options mentioned include 50 feet from all non-right-of-way property lines and 100 feet from public roads (centerline), but these do not pertain to dwellings.

The maximum total height of any turbine shall be five hundred (500) feet. This applies to Large Wind Energy Conversion Systems (Large WECS), which include systems typically defined as Wind Farms (two or more large wind systems).
Audible sound from a Large WECS facility shall not exceed fifty-five (55) dBA, as measured from any Occupied Building of a Non-Participating Landowner(s).

section: 5.78 WE-01: Wind Energy Conversion Systems: Large Wind Energy Systems
nrel_summary: All Large WECS shall meet the following setback requirements: Side and Rear Setbacks: All Large WECS shall be set back a minimum distance of 1.1 times the total height from the rear and side property lines, including all blades and attachments as certified by an Indiana licensed engineer, unless two (2) adjoining parcel owners agree to allow the tower to be constructed without a side yard setback. Front Setback: Large WECS shall be set back a minimum distance of one (1) times the total height from the right-of-way or proposed right-of-way. Large WECS shall be set back from the boundaries of any minor subdivision approved and recorded between 1992 and 2007 a minimum distance of 1,000 feet. Large WECs shall be set back from the boundaries of any subdivision, school and/or place of worship a minimum distance of 3000 feet.

section: 5.78 WE-01: Wind Energy Conversion Systems: Large Wind Energy Systems
nrel_summary: All WECS shall be designed such that shadow flicker will not fall on, or in any existing occupied building. Shadow flicker expected to fall on a roadway or a portion of a residence parcel may be acceptable under certain conditions, but if shadow flicker exceeds these conditions, the source WECS shall be shut down until the flicker is remedied. The most restrictive limit is zero hours per year on any existing occupied building.

section: 5.78 WE-01: Wind Energy Conversion Systems: Large Wind Energy Systems
nrel_summary: The minimum setback from all existing or proposed primary and accessory structures shall be two times the total height of WECS. Large WECS shall not be located within the boundaries of any recorded residential Subdivision. Audible sound from a Large WECS facility shall not exceed fifty-five (55) dBA, as measured from any Occupied Building of a Non-Participating Landowner(s). All WECS shall be designed such that shadow flicker will not fall on, or in any existing occupied building, with limited exceptions.

Sound levels under normal operating conditions of the ground-mounted solar PV installation measured at the boundary of the lot on which the installation is sited shall not be more than 10 decibels greater than would otherwise exist in the absence of the facility. The unit is expressed as decibels, assumed to be dBA as the standard unit for noise measurement.

value: ['VR: Village Residential District', 'VM: Village Mixed District', 'RU: Rural District']
section: SECTION 3 - SCHEDULE OF USE REGULATIONS, Section 3.2 Business Uses; SECTION 7 – SPECIAL OVERLAY DISTRICTS, Section 7.4 Solar Photovoltaic Overlay District; Section 9.30 Ground-mounted Solar Photovoltaic Installation requirements
nrel_summary: The Use Table in Section 3.2 Business Uses states that Ground-mounted Commercial Solar Photovoltaic Installations larger than 20 acres are 'N' (Not Permitted) in VR, VM, and RU districts. Section 9.30-2 clarifies that commercial ground-mounted PV installations larger than 20 acres require a special permit only in the Solar Photovoltaic Overlay District (SPOD), implying they are not allowed unconditionally outside the SPOD. The SPOD is intended to allow large-scale commercial ground-mounted solar installations with additional regulations, while the underlying districts VR, VM, and RU prohibit such large installations unconditionally.

The setbacks for ground-mounted solar PV installations, including appurtenant structures and parking areas, shall be at least 50 feet from any property boundary. The setback areas shall not be included in the calculation of the size of the ground-mounted solar PV installation. (Section 9.30-8.1) This applies to commercial ground-mounted solar photovoltaic installations larger than 20 acres in the Solar Photovoltaic Overlay District (SPOD). No multiplier or variable setback based on height or other factors is mentioned.

For Type III, Community Solar Installation (CSI) in the Rural District, 'System Coverage shall not exceed 20%' and 'System Area shall not exceed 35% of a parcel if the property is located within the Watershed Overlay District.' The coverage limits are expressed as percentages of the parcel area. The most restrictive maximum land coverage is 20%.

Total CSI System Area shall not exceed 150 acres town wide (solar already installed prior to the adoption of Local Law 3 of 2021 does not count against this allowance). Additionally, a Type III, Community Solar Installation (CSI) requires a minimum of 60 acres to qualify. System Coverage shall not exceed 20% and the System Area shall not exceed 35% of a parcel if the property is located within the Watershed Overlay District. The units for these area restrictions are acres.

value: ['All districts other than the Rural District, including Agricultural District and any others not named']
nrel_summary: Type III, Community Solar Installation (CSI) is only in the Rural District and requires a minimum of 60 acres to qualify. Any solar installation in the Agricultural District must follow NYS Department of Agriculture and Markets current guidelines for solar energy project. The text does not permit CSI in any district other than the Rural District, implying unconditioned prohibition elsewhere.
There shall be 250 feet minimum feet of separation from neighboring residences to CSI. For residences on the same property as the CSI there shall be a minimum 100 feet of separation.

No wind turbine generator(s) shall be located where the center of tower(s) is a distance of five (5) times the height of the tower from the base to the hub of the rotor from any off-site occupied residence or occupied commercial structure existing at the time of the filing of nonresidential subdivision plan, unless the owner of such existing residential or commercial structure shall have executed a non-disturbance easement, covenant or consent which has been recorded.

The operating WEF sound shall not exceed 35 dBA (Leq) or 50 dBC (Leq) for more than five consecutive minutes during a representative range of operating and atmospheric conditions which includes full power operation during periods when surface winds are under 2 m/s (6.6 ft/s). Further, at no time shall the sound pressure level exceed these limits by more than 5 dB. Additionally, noise levels shall not exceed the pre-operational baseline background sound levels (L90) by more than 6 dBA at any location beyond a 100 meter radius of a wind turbine tower to protect soundscape and wildlife. Instrumentation and measurement procedures must meet ANSI or IEC Type 1 standards and relevant ANSI standards for environmental sound measurement.

Minimum Wind Turbine Setback from all surrounding property lines of parcels not included in the project ... (100 kw or more) 1.5 feet for each foot of height ... To demonstrate compliance with the setback requirements ... circles drawn around each proposed tower site having a radius equal to: Five times the total height of the proposed WECS ... Height is measured from the lowest adjacent grade to the highest point of the structure, including any attachments (such as a lightening protection device or a turbine rotor or tip of the turbine blade when it reaches its highest elevation).

Minimum Wind Turbine Setback from any vacant or occupied dwelling unit on parcels not included in the project is 1.5 feet for each foot of height. Height is measured from the lowest adjacent grade to the highest point of the structure, including any attachments such as the turbine rotor or tip of the turbine blade when it reaches its highest elevation. No portion of any wind turbine blade shall be closer than 25 feet to any portion of the ground that surrounds any WEF.

In the Agricultural District, 'No more than 50% of the parcel may be used for development of the PSES.' This is the explicit maximum land coverage allowed for Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES). The unit is expressed as a percentage of the parcel area. Other related restrictions include minimum lot size of 25 acres, setbacks, and slope limitations, but these do not specify maximum land coverage.

The ordinance states under § 1704, Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES), subsection F, Dimensional Requirements: 'Maximum Height: 20 feet at maximum tilt.' This applies to ground-mounted PSES. For roof- and wall-mounted PSES, the height 'shall be subject to the maximum height regulations of the underlying zoning district.' The explicit numerical maximum height given is 20 feet, and the unit is feet.

The ordinance states under § 1704, section 1.F 'Dimensional Requirements' that the minimum setbacks for Principal Solar Energy Systems (PSES) are '50 feet (front, rear and side)'. Other related provisions include a minimum lot size of 25 acres and that no more than 50% of the parcel may be used for development of the PSES. The fence enclosing the PSES must also meet setback requirements for the use. The ordinance also mentions a 150-foot setback from the nearest occupied residential building on a nonparticipating landowner's property, but this setback is from a structure, not a property line or parcel boundary, and thus not included here.

Solar panels shall be set back from the nearest occupied residential building located on a nonparticipating landowners property, a distance of not less than 150 feet measured from the outer edge of the solar panel nearest to the occupied building to the nearest point on the foundation of the occupied building. Other dimensional requirements include a minimum setback of 50 feet (front, rear and side) for PSES, but the 150 feet setback from occupied residential buildings on nonparticipating properties is the more specific and restrictive requirement.

Section 300.1151 D.3 states: 'All photovoltaic panels located on a solar farm shall be restricted to a maximum design height of 16 feet.' This applies specifically to solar farms defined as land primarily designated or used for producing solar electricity sold or transferred to electric companies or third parties, occupying 10,000 square feet or more of panel area. Other height restrictions mentioned include a 6-foot minimum height for security fencing and an 18-foot limit for light poles, but these do not apply to the solar panels themselves. The unit for the height restriction is feet.

The noise from a solar farm shall not exceed 55 decibels as measured at any property line. This applies specifically to Solar Farms as defined in the ordinance: "Solar Farm: Land primarily designated or used for the purpose of producing solar or photovoltaic electricity... The power generated is sold or transferred to electric companies or other third parties for distribution through a power grid..." The unit is expressed as decibels, and for the purposes of this extraction, the standard unit for noise is 'dBA'.

section: 300.1151 SOLAR FARMS AND SOLAR PANELS, Subsection D.4. Setbacks
nrel_summary: All photovoltaic solar panels and support structures associated with solar farms (excluding perimeter security fencing) shall be a minimum of 20 feet from any side or rear property line. Other setbacks mentioned include a minimum of 50 feet from any road or highway right-of-way or easement, but this does not pertain to property lines, lot lines, facility perimeters, parcels, or subdivisions.

The maximum Total Height of any WECS shall be 420 feet. This applies to Large WECS as defined in the ordinance, which includes systems with a total height of more than 150 feet and rated capacity greater than 250 kilowatts intended primarily to supply electrical power into a power grid for sale.

The statistical sound pressure level generated by a WECS shall not exceed L10 – 50 dBA measured at the closest exterior wall of any residence existing at the time of completing the SEQRA review of the application. If the ambient sound pressure level exceeds 50 dBA, the standard shall be ambient dBA plus 5 dBA.

Each WECS shall be setback from Site boundaries, measured from the center of the WECS, a minimum distance of: Setbacks from adjacent property lines, rights-of-way, easements, public ways or power lines (not to include individual residential feed line) shall be one and one-half times the maximum structure height or 1 ¾ times the maximum engineer-calculated ice or blade throw distance to the maximum point of impact, whichever is greater.

Each WECS shall be setback from Site boundaries, measured from the center of the WECS, a minimum distance of 1,000 feet from the nearest off-Site Residence existing at the time of application, measured from the exterior of such residence.

All ground arrays shall be set back a distance of 1.1 times the structure height from all property lines in a residential district or in conformance with the bulk standards for accessory structures in nonresidential districts as provided herein. No static distance value is added to this multiplier. Ground arrays shall not be permitted in a front yard.

Section 7, item Q states: 'No solar energy farm facilities shall exceed sixty-five (65) dBA as measured at the property line.' This applies specifically to Solar Energy Farms, defined as systems primarily to generate energy for sale back into the energy grid system. The unit 'dBA' is the standard unit for noise level measurement.

Section 4(a) states that commercial wind energy devices shall be limited to a total height of 250 feet within 1,250 feet of any residential zoned district. Outside of that proximity, no height limitations apply except for restrictions related to airport airspace.

Sound produced by any wind energy devices under normal operating conditions, as measured at the property line, shall not produce sound at a level that would constitute a nuisance. Industry standards support that wind energy noise should not exceed 50 dBA at a distance of 1,250 feet, the setback distance in Emmet County to a human occupied dwelling.

section: Section 4. Wind Energy Requirements b. Setbacks.
nrel_summary: Commercial wind energy devices shall be set back a distance equal to 110% its total height from any public right of way, overhead utility lines or adjacent property lines not under the same ownership unless written consent is granted by the property owner or entity with jurisdiction over the street, utilities or adjacent properties.

section: Section 4. Wind Energy Requirements b. Setbacks.
nrel_summary: Commercial wind energy devices shall be setback a distance of no less than 1,250 feet from any human occupied dwelling. A human occupied dwelling is defined as one that is currently occupied or capable of being occupied for residential purposes. A greater setback may be required to minimize shadow flicker, nuisance noise, and other possible documented effects to humans living in these dwellings.

Wind generator machine and associated meteorological tower overall height shall not exceed six hundred (600) feet. Machine height is measured from grade to the top of the structure, including the uppermost extension of any blades for horizontal axis machines, or to the highest point of the structure for vertical axis or other machine designs.

Audible noise due to wind turbine operations shall not cause the exterior noise level to exceed forty-five (45) dBA for more than five (5) minutes out of any one- (1-) hour time period (L8.3) or to exceed fifty (50) dBA for any period of time when measured within fifty (50) feet of any existing residence, school, hospital, church, or public library. The units for noise levels are expressed in dBA.

Setback requirements for large wind energy systems specify that a minimum wind generator setback of two (2) times the overall machine height or five hundred (500) feet, whichever is less, shall be maintained from exterior project boundaries adjacent to parcels under forty (40) acres. For adjacent parcels of forty (40) acres or more, a minimum setback of one and one-half (1 1/2) times the overall machine height or five hundred (500) feet, whichever is less, shall be maintained from all exterior project boundaries.

A minimum wind generator setback of one and one-half (1 1/2) times the overall machine height or five hundred (500) feet, whichever is greater, shall be maintained from any off-site residence. A minimum wind generator setback of one (1) times the overall machine height shall be maintained from any on-site residence or accessory structure designed for human occupancy.

Audible noise due to wind farm operations shall not exceed fifty decibels (50 dBA) for any period of time when measured at any residence, school, hospital, church or public building existing on the date of Conditional Use approval of the wind farm. If the noise contains a steady pure tone, the standard shall be reduced by five decibels (5 dBA).

Each wind turbine shall be set back from the nearest property line, a distance no less than 1.1 times the total height of the tower, plus the length of the turbine blades, unless easements are secured from adjacent property owners.

Each wind turbine shall be set back from the nearest inhabited dwelling, school, hospital, church or public building, a distance no less than two (2) times the total height of the tower, plus the length of the turbine blades or 1,000 feet, whichever is greater.

Large scale wind energy conversion devices shall be set back a distance equal to at least 1.5 times the overall height of the wind energy conversion facility from the nearest property line and from the nearest private or public way street line. Any supporting structure including guy wires shall not be located closer to any property line or street line than the distance equal to the minimum building setback required for the zoning district in which the facility is located. The Planning Board may reduce the above minimum setback distances, as appropriate based on site-specific considerations, if the project satisfies all other criteria for the granting of a special permit under the provisions of this Section.

The ordinance states that any ten (10) minute LAeq shall not exceed forty-five (45) dB(A) at the property line of a non-participating parcel(s) boundary. Sound level limits are to be evaluated using the A-weighted equivalent sound level (LAeq) descriptor, measured using ten-minute time intervals.
All Utility-Scale WES shall be setback from non-participating parcel property lines a distance of no less than two times the height of the wind turbine tower.

A Utility-Scale WES shall be designed, sited, operated, and equipped with proven technology to minimize shadow flicker. Utility-Scale WES shall be placed such that shadow flicker to any occupied buildings occurs no more than 30 hours per year. Shadow Flicker in excess of 30 hours per year must be mitigated or eliminated.

All Utility-Scale WES shall be setback from the nearest non-participating parcel, school, hospital, church or public library, or any other occupied buildings a distance of no less than one thousand five hundred (1,500) feet. Any structure above constructed after the approval of a WES on a Participating or Non-Participating Parcel, shall not be required to meet the minimum setback.

No structure shall be located or operated so that the noise level at any existing residence or residential district or business or other enterprise shall exceed 50 decibels for the entire site or interfere with normal sleep patterns. The noise level is expressed in decibels (dBA).
No structure shall be located within 500 feet of any residence, residential district, church or school.

Ground-mounted SES cannot exceed a height of 15 feet. The height is measured from the finished grade below the panel to the top of the panel at its highest tilt. Building-mounted SES cannot exceed the height limits for buildings of an underlying zoning district.

The ordinance states under section D.2.c. Overlay Rezone Prerequisites: 'Minimum Project Acreage: 5 acres. Maximum Project Acreage: 400 acres.' This maximum project acreage of 400 acres applies specifically to Commercial Solar Energy Systems (SES) projects subject to rezoning into the Energy Overlay District, which is required for Commercial SES. The units for the maximum lot size are expressed in acres.

The ordinance states: 'SES may not produce noise that exceeds forty-five decibels (45 dBA) measured at any point along the site’s property line.' This maximum noise level applies explicitly to Commercial Solar Energy Systems (SES) as defined and regulated in the ordinance. No other noise level values or conditions for Commercial SES noise limits are provided.

The minimum distance between a Commercial Solar Energy System (SES) structure and any property lot line of a non-participating property is 1,000 feet. Other setback distances include 500 feet from participating property lot lines and 2 miles from corporate boundaries (municipalities). The ordinance states: 'ii) Non-Participating Property. The minimum distance between a SES structure and any property lot line of a non-participating property is 1,000 feet.'

Section 5.30.2.4 states a maximum height of 150 feet for Wind Energy Systems, which are defined as electric generating complexes of wind towers supplying electricity to the power grid. This is the explicit maximum turbine height allowed for Wind Energy Facilities. The units are feet as indicated in the text.
Audible sound from a Wind Energy Facility shall not exceed fifty (55) dBA, as measured at the exterior of any Occupied Building on a Non-participating Landowner’s property.

Wind Energy Systems are prohibited in all zoning districts except the Conservation (C) and Conservation Sinks (CS) Districts (§5.30.1). This prohibition applies generally and unconditionally, with no expiration date specified. Permits are required for construction and operation within allowed districts (§5.30.2.3).

section: Section 25. Placeriement, Paragraph C. Industrial WTG Noise Level Limit
nrel_summary: An Industrial WTG shall be designed, installed, and operated so that noise generated by the system shall not exceed 50 decibels (dBA), as measured at the closest neighboring inhabited dwelling, except during short-term events including utility outages and severe wind storms.

Each IWTG shall be located with the following minimum setbacks, as measured from the center of the IWTG. Structure height shall be measured from the ground surface level to the maximum height of the blades above the nacelle. 1.5 times the IWTG Total Height from Property Lines. The property lines setback requirement may be reduced by the Town Board/Planning Board as an incident of special permit review when the Town Board/Planning Board finds the following: (i) both properties on each side of the property line in question will have electric generation or transmission facilities constructed on them as part of the project review, or (ii) the owner of the property for which the reduced setback is sought executes and presents for recording a development easement satisfactory to the Town Board/Planning Board in which the reduced setback is consented to, and construction within, and use of the easement area is appropriately restricted.

Each IWTG shall be located with the following minimum setbacks, as measured from the center of the IWTG. Structure height shall be measured from the ground surface level to the maximum height of the blades above the nacelle. 1. 1400 feet or 2 times the IWTG Total Height whichever is greater, from offsite residences measured from the closest exterior wall. 5. 1.5 times the IWTG Total Height from off site permanent structures.

section: 6. Setbacks — Wind Turbines and Meteorological towers
nrel_summary: The setback for commercial wind turbines from property lines is 1.25 times the total height or the distance of the fall zone as certified by a professional engineer, plus 25 feet.

section: 6. Setbacks — Wind Turbines and Meteorological towers
nrel_summary: The setback for dwellings shall be reciprocal in that no dwelling shall be constructed within 1000 feet of a commercial wind turbine. Setbacks are described as 'Certified by a professional engineer + 25 feet or 1.25 times the total height.' The 'total height' is defined as the highest point above ground level reached by a rotor tip or any other part of the WECS. The ordinance uses a multiplier of 1.25 times the total height (tip height) to compute setback distances from occupied dwellings, buildings, structures, and/or residences for Commercial WECS.

section: U. Solar energy system, large scale
nrel_summary: The height of the Large-scale solar energy systems shall not exceed fifteen (15) feet when oriented at maximum tilt. (Section U.(3)(a)) This is the explicit maximum structure height restriction for large-scale solar energy systems. Other height limits mentioned in the text apply to small-scale or subdivision solar energy systems, or general building height limits in various zoning districts, and are not applicable to large-scale solar energy systems. The unit 'feet' is explicitly stated in the ordinance.

section: U. Solar energy system, large scale
nrel_summary: The maximum area for a large-scale solar energy system shall be twenty (20) acres. This is explicitly stated in section (3)(b) under 'U. Solar energy system, large scale.' The unit is acres, a standard area measurement. Other lot size limits mentioned, such as two (2) acres, apply only to subdivision solar energy systems, which are distinct from large-scale systems.

section: U. Solar energy system, large scale.
nrel_summary: The ordinance states in section U.(4)(a): 'Solar systems which export energy shall not be permitted in any National or New York State Designated Historic District, or in the Ridge Protection District.' Large-scale solar energy systems are permitted through special use permits in the RU (Rural) and PCIM (Planned Commercial, Industrial & Mixed Uses) districts, and are also listed as special uses in the RED (Resort and Economic Development) district. Other districts mention only small-scale solar energy systems or do not explicitly address large-scale systems. Therefore, the Ridge Protection District (RP) is the only district where large-scale solar energy systems are unconditionally prohibited.

section: U. Solar energy system, large scale (3)(a) and V. Solar Energy System, subdivision (2)(b)
nrel_summary: With the exception of underground conduits, all structures shall be set back no less than 100 feet from all property lines. For subdivision solar energy systems, all components of the system, except for underground utility lines, shall be set back 100 feet from any property line.

section: C. Development Standards for Commercial WECS
nrel_summary: The maximum total height of any wind turbine within a Commercial WECS shall be five hundred (500) feet.

section: SECTION F. Noise Standards for Wind Energy Conversion Systems
nrel_summary: The Sound Level statistical sound pressure level (L)(10) due to any Commercial WECS operation shall not exceed ambient noise levels by more than 5 dBA at the nearest lot line.

Structures and wind turbines for Commercial WECS shall be set back from lot lines, measured from the center of the applicable component part of the Commercial WECS the following minimum distances: 1. 1250 feet from off site lot lines;

section: Town of Great Valley Zoning Law                    Districts and Regulations
nrel_summary: The Town of Great Valley Zoning Law prohibits Commercial-scale Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS), defined as Utility-Scale WECS intended solely to generate electrical power for sale to the power grid, in all listed zoning districts (AR, HRC, C-I, RR, HD) as indicated by 'NP' (Not Permitted). There are no conditions or expiration dates associated with this prohibition.

section: § 179-97 Permitting requirements for Tier 3 solar energy systems
nrel_summary: For Tier 3 solar energy systems located on areas that consist of prime farmland or farmland of statewide importance, the system shall not exceed 50% of the area of prime farmland or farmland of statewide importance on the parcel. Additionally, lot coverage of the solar energy system components shall not exceed the maximum lot coverage requirement of the underlying zoning district. The 50% limit is a specific numerical maximum land coverage value explicitly stated, while the lot coverage limit depends on zoning district standards. The units for the 50% limit are expressed as a percentage of the total land area.

section: § 179-97 Permitting requirements for Tier 3 solar energy systems.
nrel_summary: All Tier 3 solar energy systems are permitted through the issuance of a special use permit pursuant to § 179-24 of this chapter within the Industrial (I-1), Light Industrial (I-2) and General Commercial (C-1) zoning districts, and are subject to site plan application requirements set forth in Article VI of this chapter. The text does not explicitly list districts where Tier 3 solar energy systems are unconditionally prohibited, but by permitting Tier 3 systems only in I-1, I-2, and C-1 districts, it implies prohibition in all other districts. For comparison, Tier 1 solar energy systems are permitted in all zoning districts and exempt from site plan review, and Tier 2 solar energy systems are permitted in all zoning districts as accessory structures and exempt from site plan review, subject to conditions.

section: Sec. 66-1213. - Large wind energy conversion systems—Height and setbacks.
nrel_summary: The wind turbine height of a large system shall not exceed 500 feet or the height recommended by the manufacturer or distributor of the system, whichever is lesser. The board of supervisors may allow a project to exceed this height restriction if certain criteria are met.

section: Sec. 66-1214. - Large wind energy conversion systems—Environmental.
nrel_summary: Large systems shall not exceed 60 decibels or other more stringent standard otherwise applicable as measured at the closest non-participating property line. An analysis, prepared by a qualified acoustical engineer, shall be provided by the applicant to demonstrate compliance with the standard for sound emission.

section: Sec. 66-1213. - Large wind energy conversion systems—Height and setbacks.
nrel_summary: The wind energy conversion system shall be set back from all adjoining nonparticipating property lines a distance at least equal to 125 percent of the wind turbine height. Setbacks shall be measured from the outside surface at the base of the wind energy tower and in a horizontal direction. These setbacks may be reduced by notarized consent of the adjoining landowner and execution of a deed of easement prohibiting construction of new structures within the setback area.

section: Sec. 66-1213. - Large wind energy conversion systems—Height and setbacks.
nrel_summary: The wind energy conversion system shall be set back a distance equal to 160 percent of the wind turbine height or 800 feet, whichever is greater, from any occupied building or public use area. These setbacks may be reduced by notarized consent of the owner of the property on which the requested wind energy conversion system is to be erected and the adjoining landowner whose dwelling falls within the setback area, along with a deed of easement prohibiting construction of any new structure within the setback area. Large systems shall meet all setback requirements for primary structures for the zoning district in which the wind energy conversion system is located in addition to the requirements set forth above. The setbacks shall be kept free of all habitable structures or occupied buildings so long as the facility is in place; setbacks shall be measured from the outside surface at the base of the wind energy tower and in a horizontal direction.

Noise emanating from the operation of a LWET shall not exceed, at any time, the lowest ambient sound level that is present between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 9:00 a.m. at any property line of a residential or agricultural use parcel or from the property line of parks, schools, hospitals, and churches. Noise emanating from the operation of a LWET(s) shall not exceed, at the time, the lowest ambient noise level plus 5 dBA that is present between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 9:00 a.m. at any property line of a non-residential or non-agricultural use parcel. Methods for measuring and reporting acoustic emissions from Wind Turbines and the Wind Energy Facility shall be equal to or exceed the minimum standards for precision described in AWEA Standard 2.1 - 1989 titled Procedures for the Measurement and Reporting of Acoustic emissions from Wind Turbine Generation Systems Volume 1: First Tier.

The setback distance for Large Wind Energy Turbines (LWET) is determined by taking the maximum of a fixed threshold value and a multiplier of the turbine's total height, as stated: 'Each LWET shall be set back from the nearest Occupied Building that is located on the same parcel as the LWET a minimum of two (2) times its Total Height, or one thousand (1,000) feet, as measured from the base of the Tower, whichever is greater.' Additionally, 'the internal property line setbacks shall be a minimum of one and one-half (1.5) times the Total Height, as measured from the base of the Tower,' which may be reduced only with engineer certification. Along the border of the Wind Energy Overlay District, there shall be a setback distance equal to two (2) times the Total Height. These provisions establish firm minimum setbacks that must be met in all cases.

Shadow Flicker: The MWET or LWET owner(s) and/or operators) shall conduct an analysis on potential shadow flicker at any occupied building with direct line-of-sight to the MWET or LWET. The analysis shall identify the locations of shadow flicker that may be caused by the project and the expected durations of the flicker at these locations from sun-rise to sun-set over the course of a year. The analysis shall identify situations where shadow flicker may affect the occupants of the buildings for more than 30 hours per year, and describe measures that shall be taken to eliminate or mitigate the problems. Shadow Flicker on a building shall not exceed thirty (30) hours per year.

Each LWET shall be set back from the nearest Occupied Building that is located on the same parcel as the LWET a minimum of two (2) times its Total Height, or one thousand (1,000) feet, as measured from the base of the Tower, whichever is greater.

section: § 340-3.24 Requirements for all nonaccessory ground-mounted solar photovoltaic systems
nrel_summary: The maximum height of any component or appurtenance structure of the ground-mounted solar photovoltaic system shall be 15 feet. This applies to all nonaccessory ground-mounted solar photovoltaic systems, which include utility-scale systems intended for selling energy and energy credits to third parties. The relevant text is from § 340-3.24, subsection J: 'The maximum height of any component or appurtenance structure of the ground-mounted solar photovoltaic system shall be 15 feet.' No other more restrictive height limits for utility-scale systems are provided. The unit is explicitly stated as feet.

section: § 340-3.24 Requirements for all nonaccessory ground-mounted solar photovoltaic systems
nrel_summary: For nonaccessory ground-mounted solar photovoltaic systems (which include utility-scale systems), the ordinance states: 'Noise generation. Solar photovoltaic systems shall not generate noise above ambient beyond a lot line on which a solar photovoltaic system is installed. Specifically, there shall be a 0 dB increase over the ambient levels at the applicant's property boundary lines.' Ambient sound is determined with preapplication acoustical testing and confirmed post-installation. Testing costs are borne by the applicant/owner-operator. The unit is expressed as decibels (dB).

section: § 340-3.24 Requirements for all nonaccessory ground-mounted solar photovoltaic systems
nrel_summary: All solar arrays must be set back a minimum of 100 feet from property lines (§ 340-3.24D(1)). All components of the solar photovoltaic system shall be set back from the property line a minimum of 100 feet, with a permanent all-season green buffer planted within this setback (§ 340-3.24G). In the Solar Photovoltaic Overlay District (SPOD), a setback of 100 feet shall apply and be measured from the Overlay Zone line (§ 340-3.30C(2)). These setbacks apply to nonaccessory (utility-scale) ground-mounted solar photovoltaic systems defined as systems for selling energy and exceeding six acres and 30% of the gross lot area. No height-based multiplier is applied; setbacks are fixed distances.
Any wind turbine within a wind farm shall be located not less than the Rotor Radius from property lines abutting non-participating properties.

No commercial wind turbine shall be located at a distance less than 1000 Feet from the nearest occupied dwelling. Wind generator towers may be setback less than 1000 feet from a dwelling if the property owner signs a waiver agreeing to the reduced setback distance. However, the wind generator tower shall not be located closer than the distance equal to the height of the tower.

Wind turbines for electrical generation are prohibited in any residential district within the corporate city limits of Hallsville and allowed only in the Light Industrial (LI) District by Conditional Use Permit (CUP). The prohibition in residential districts is absolute and has no expiration date.

Section 8, Standards for Large WECS, subsection N states: 'Maximum Total Height of any WECS shall be 500 feet.' This is the explicit maximum turbine height allowed for Large Wind Energy Conversion Systems (Large WECS) in the Town of Edwards.

The statistical sound pressure level (L10) generated by a WECS shall not exceed 45 dBA when measured at the nearest inhabited off-site dwelling, school, hospital, church, or public building existing at the time of application. If the ambient sound pressure level exceeds 50 dBA, the standard shall be ambient dBA plus 5 dBA. Independent certification shall be provided before and after construction demonstrating compliance with this requirement.

section: Section 11. Setbacks for Wind Energy Conversion Systems
nrel_summary: Each WECS shall be setback from Site boundaries, measured from the center of the WECS: 1. 500 feet from the nearest site boundary property line. 3. 500 feet from the nearest edge of the Wind Overlay District. 5. One and a half times the Total Height of the WECS from any non-WECS structure or any above-ground utilities.

section: Setbacks for Wind Energy Conversion Systems
nrel_summary: Each WECS shall be setback 1,000 feet from the nearest off-site residence existing at the time of application, measured from the exterior of such residence, and one and a half times the Total Height of the WECS from any non-WECS structure or any above-ground utilities.
The maximum height of a wind turbine or meteorological tower shall be 150 feet, as measured from the ground to the highest point of the blade or tower.

Section 9.13.7 states that 'Wind turbines shall not exceed 55 decibels (dBA) as measured at the property line.' This is the maximum noise level allowed for large wind energy systems, with units explicitly given as dBA.

Wind turbines and meteorological towers shall be set back from all property lines a distance equal to 1.5 times the total height of the structure, as measured from the ground to the highest point of the blade or tower.

Wind turbines and meteorological towers shall be set back from occupied buildings a distance equal to 1.5 times the total height of the structure, as measured from the ground to the highest point of the blade or tower.

section: SECTION 5: GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR COMMERCIAL GRADE WIND ENERGY CONVERSION SYSTEMS AND METEOROLOGICAL TOWERS
nrel_summary: Section 5, subsection D states: 'Maximum Height: WEDs and METs shall not exceed six hundred fifty (650) feet in total height.' This applies to Wind Energy Devices that are part of a Commercial Grade Wind Energy Conversion System (C-WECS).

section: SECTION 5: GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR COMMERCIAL GRADE WIND ENERGY CONVERSION SYSTEMS AND METEOROLOGICAL TOWERS
nrel_summary: No more than one hundred fifty (150) Wind Energy Devices shall be allowed in Fremont County, Iowa. This sets a clear maximum number of turbines allowed for Commercial Grade Wind Energy Conversion Systems (C-WECS) projects in the jurisdiction.

section: SECTION 5: GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR COMMERCIAL GRADE WIND ENERGY CONVERSION SYSTEMS AND METEOROLOGICAL TOWERS
nrel_summary: Sound produced by any WED under normal operating conditions as measured at the exterior wall of a residence shall not exceed 50 dBA. Sound levels may be exceeded during short term events out of the Owner/Developer/Operator’s control, such as utility outages and/or severe wind or weather conditions.

section: SECTION 5: GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR COMMERCIAL GRADE WIND ENERGY CONVERSION SYSTEMS AND METEOROLOGICAL TOWERS
nrel_summary: The setback distance from a Non-Participating Property Line for Commercial Grade Wind Energy Conversion Systems (C-WECS) is 1.1 times the Total Height of the Wind Energy Device (WED). This setback is measured from the nearest point of the property line to the center point of the foundation of the WED at natural ground level. No additional static distance is added to this multiplier.

section: SECTION 4: WIND ENERGY CONVERSION SYSTEM PERMIT APPLICATION and SECTION 5: GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR COMMERCIAL GRADE WIND ENERGY CONVERSION SYSTEMS AND METEOROLOGICAL TOWERS
nrel_summary: The ordinance requires that no non-participating residence will experience more than 30 hours per year of shadow flicker under planned operating conditions for Commercial Grade Wind Energy Conversion Systems (C-WECS). If this threshold is exceeded, the Owner/Developer/Operator must mitigate the shadow flicker to comply with the ordinance.

section: SECTION 5: GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR COMMERCIAL GRADE WIND ENERGY CONVERSION SYSTEMS AND METEOROLOGICAL TOWERS
nrel_summary: For non-participating residences, the setback is 1,500 feet for smaller turbines and 1,600 feet for larger turbines. These setbacks apply to all Wind Energy Devices (WEDs) and are measured from the nearest point of the residence to the center point of the foundation of the WED at natural ground level. Additionally, above ground Wind Energy Accessory Buildings or Structures shall be set back no less than 1,500 feet from any residential dwelling unless the property owner provides written consent.

section: §100-5.8 D Solar Energy Farm Site Requirements
nrel_summary: The total surface area of all ground-mounted and freestanding solar collectors, including solar voltaic cells, panels and arrays, shall not exceed 80% of the total parcel area. This is the maximum land coverage allowed for Solar Energy Farms exceeding six (6) acres. The unit is expressed as a percentage of the total parcel area.
All solar energy system components shall have a 50 foot setback, unless abutting residential uses. Whereby it shall be located a minimum of 200’ from property lines.

No portion of the facility shall be within one-half mile of properties zoned residential use or designated on a comprehensive plan as residential. If the facility is located in a residential zone then this restriction does not apply to the lot or parcel that the facility is located on, or any adjacent property in common ownership.

No portion of the facility shall be within one-half mile of properties zoned residential use or designated on a comprehensive plan as residential. Towers and turbines shall not be constructed closer than one-half mile of an existing residence unless a written waiver is obtained from the landowner.

No Commercial/Utility WECS shall exceed 50 dBA as measured at the closest neighboring inhabited dwelling unit. Exception: a Commercial/Utility WECS may exceed 50 dBA during periods of severe weather as defined by the US Weather Service.

Setbacks for Commercial/Utility WECS from property lines require a distance of '4.1 times the total height plus applicable building setback' or 'Diameter plus applicable building setback.' The 'total height' is defined as the highest point above ground level reached by a rotor tip. The 'applicable building setback' is an additional static distance added to these calculations. All towers shall adhere to the setbacks established in Table 1. Property Line is defined as the boundary line of the area over which the entity applying for a Wind Energy Conversion System permit has legal control.

section: Article 25 Supplemental District Regulations — Section 23 Wind Energy Conversion Facilities
nrel_summary: The setback from neighboring dwelling units for Commercial/Utility WECS is 1.1 times the total height plus applicable building setback. The setback for dwelling units shall be reciprocal in that no dwelling unit shall be constructed within the same distance required for a commercial/utility Wind Energy Conversion System. All towers shall adhere to the setbacks established in Table 1.

Solar Energy Facilities with nameplate capacity of 250 kW or greater shall be sited by Special Permit only in the RR, RN and G zoning districts. One Solar Energy Facility with nameplate capacity of 250 kW or greater for municipal government purposes is allowed "As of Right" on one selected parcel of Town-owned land. The bylaw does not explicitly prohibit these facilities in any district unconditionally. Other solar energy systems with less than 250 kW capacity also require a Special Permit. Ground-mounted Solar Energy Facilities are allowed in all districts if the energy is primarily for on-premise use and conforms to yard requirements, but those used primarily off-premises require a Special Permit in all districts.

Setbacks for Large-Scale Ground-Mounted Solar Energy Facilities are fixed distances from property lines, lot lines, and facility perimeters. Specifically, "Solar arrays and related equipment shall have front, side and rear yard setbacks of a minimum of 100 feet." However, "If a front, side or rear lot line abuts one or more residences, the setback for that lot line shall be a minimum of 200 feet." Other setback distances include "front, side and rear yard setbacks of at least 50 feet for any fencing that is required" and "Setback from a public way shall be at least 200 feet." Additionally, "A 50-foot minimum setback shall apply when the abutting parcel has the same owner and the same proposed use as that for the proposed facility." The Zoning Board of Appeals may allow lesser or require greater setbacks based on potential impacts.

The ordinance requires that if a front, side or rear lot line abuts one or more residences, the setback for that lot line shall be a minimum of 200 feet. Other setback options include: 100 feet minimum front, side and rear yard setbacks for solar arrays and related equipment; 50 feet minimum setbacks for fencing enclosing the facility; 50 feet minimum setback when the abutting parcel has the same owner and use as the proposed facility. The Zoning Board of Appeals may allow lesser or greater setbacks based on potential impacts. (See Sections 3.28.10.A.1-7)

Structures shall not exceed twenty-five (25) feet in height, as measured from grade at the base of the structure to its highest point. This applies to Solar Energy Facilities, which include solar farms generating photovoltaic power for an area greater than the principal use on the site. The text also mentions a height limit of two hundred (200) feet for Wind Energy Facilities, but the 25 feet limit is the most restrictive for solar energy systems.

The buffer shall be required around the entire perimeter of the footprint of the Solar Farm. The buffer options are: 1) A ten (10) foot opaque fence with six (6) feet minimum height evergreen plantings every ten (10) feet, with plantings located within six (6) feet of the fence on the outer portion; or 2) An existing 100-foot wide natural buffer capable of encompassing the entire footprint of the solar farm. The 10-foot fence option is the more restrictive fixed distance setback.

Each wind turbine shall be set back from the wind energy facility perimeter at a distance not less than 5 (five) times the rotor diameter of the wind turbine. The wind energy facility perimeter is defined as the boundary of the wind energy facility as defined by the external property lines of landowners who have a contractual relationship with the Permitee.

Each wind turbine shall be set back from the nearest occupied dwelling, commercial building or publicly-used structure or facility at a distance not less than 1.25 times its total height or 750 feet, whichever is greater.

section: 301.6. Alternative Energy Sources and 304.1. Height Limit Exceptions
nrel_summary: Height regulations do not apply to WECS units, provided that the height of the WECS unit shall not be greater than the shortest distance measured along a horizontal plane from the unit to any lot line. The height regulations listed in Article 2 do not apply to ... wind energy conversion systems ... provided such structures ... are set back a horizontal distance at least equal to their height from any property line or right-of-way line, plus fifteen (15) feet.

Noise immissions from the operation of a WECS shall not exceed 45 decibels on the dB(A) scale during 7 am to 7 pm MDT, and 40 decibels on the dB(A) scale during 7 pm to 7 am MDT. In addition, noise immissions shall not exceed 50 decibels on the dB(C) scale during 7 pm to 7 am. Such noise immissions shall be measured at the nearest receiving property or lot line not owned or leased to the WECS owner/operator. The most restrictive maximum noise level is 40 dBA at night.

The setback from the WECS Facility Boundary Line for Commercial WECS Facilities with 30 or more WECS Towers is one and one-half times the Wind Generation Device Height or a minimum distance of 1,600 feet, whichever distance is greater. Setbacks shall be measured from the center of the Wind Generation Device foundation. For Any Platted Subdivision and County Residential Zone District and any City and Town, the minimum setback is one and one-quarter miles. A waiver from the setback requirements shall run with the land and be recorded as part of the chain of title for the subject property.

section: Section 17. 4. Commercial WECS Setbacks and Standards
nrel_summary: The minimum setback distance for Commercial WECS Facilities from occupied dwellings, buildings, structures, and/or residences is "Five and one-half times the Wind Generation Device Height or one-half mile, whichever distance is greater." This means the setback distance must be at least one-half mile (2,640 feet) or 5.5 times the turbine height, whichever is greater.

section: ARTICLE 31: SUPPLEMENTARY USE REGULATIONS CONDITIONAL USES, ACCESSORY USES, PRHOBITED USES
nrel_summary: Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems are specifically prohibited in Wabaunsee County. No application for such a use shall be considered, effectively setting the maximum allowable project size or total installation at zero systems (a count, not measured in units).

section: ARTICLE 31: SUPPLEMENTARY USE REGULATIONS CONDITIONAL USES, ACCESSORY USES, PRHOBITED USES
nrel_summary: Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems are specifically prohibited as a use in Wabaunsee County. They are not a use that may be approved or permitted as a Conditional Use, and no application for such a use shall be considered. No expiration date or conditions for this prohibition are provided.

section: ARTICLE 31: SUPPLEMENTARY USE REGULATIONS CONDITIONAL USES, ACCESSORY USES, PRHOBITED USES
nrel_summary: Commercial Wind Energy Conversion Systems are specifically prohibited as a use in Wabaunsee County. No Commercial Wind Energy Conversion System shall be placed in Wabaunsee County, and no application for such a use shall be considered. This prohibition effectively sets the maximum shadow flicker allowed to 0 hr/year for these systems.
No wind tower total height shall exceed 500 feet. This is the maximum feasible height for Commercial/Industrial Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS) in the Town of Randolph.

section: 27. Noise Standards for Wind Energy Systems
nrel_summary: Noise standards are based on: a sound pressure level limit of 45 dB(A) in Residential Districts, which may be exceeded by 10 dB(A) for a single period no longer than 15 minutes in any one day. Noise shall be measured with an approved sound level meter using procedures meeting ANSI standards and approved by the Town of Randolph. Noise below 20 Hz (infrasound) is not permitted, and tonal noises such as whine, screech, or hum shall be eliminated.

section: G. Standards for Commercial/Industrial WECS - 2. Setbacks
nrel_summary: From property lines: A minimum 1500 feet or 2 times the total WECS height from any property line excluding adjoining lot lines of the project participants. Such setbacks from property lines do not apply if the application is accompanied by a legally enforceable agreement recorded in the Cattaraugus County Clerk’s Office for a period of the life of the permit, that the affected adjacent landowner(s) agree to the elimination of the setback.

Setbacks for Commercial/Industrial Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS) require a minimum distance of 2000 feet or a multiplier of the total WECS height, whichever is greater, from buildings and residences. Specifically, from structures: "a minimum of 2000 feet or 2.5 times the total WECS height from any building, whichever is greater." From residences: "a minimum of three times the total WECS height or 2000 feet." These minimum distances act as thresholds that must be met in all cases.

Audible sound from a wind energy facility shall not exceed forty-five (45) dBA as measured at the exterior of any occupied building on any other parcel. Methods for measuring and reporting acoustic emissions from wind turbines and the wind energy facility shall be equal to or exceed the minimum standards for precision described in AWEA Standard 2.1. 1989 titled Procedures for the Measurement and Reporting of Acoustic Emissions from Wind Turbine Generation Systems Volume I: First Tier.

The ordinance requires that for commercial wind energy facilities, setbacks from property lines, lot lines, and parcels must be at least one and one tenth (1.1) times the total height of the wind turbine, including the rotor plane (§507.55.D.2.b and f). Additionally, if the land is leased, licensed, or under easement, all wind turbines and accessory structures must be at least thirty (30) feet from the lease, license, or easement line (§507.55.D.2.b). For horizontal rotors, setbacks must be not less than one and one tenth (1.1) times the height of the turbine tower or one and one tenth (1.1) times the height plus the rotor length, whichever is greater (§507.55.D.2.h). These setbacks act as minimum distances that must be met in all cases.

No wind turbine shall be located less than six hundred (600) feet from any existing principal structure on the wind energy facility parcel or lease, license or easement parcel as measured from the center point of the turbine base, unless the property owner provides written permission allowing for a lesser distance. In no event shall the setback distance be less than one and one tenth (1.1) times the total height of the wind turbine as measured from the highest point of the turbine, including the rotor plane. No wind turbine shall be located less than two thousand (2,000) feet from any principal structure existing on any other parcel prior to the erection of the wind turbine as measured from the center point of the turbine base, unless the owner of such existing principal structure shall have executed a written waiver or non-disturbance easement, covenant or consent. Such setback distance shall not be less than one and one tenth (1.1) times the total height of the wind turbine.

The maximum allowable height for any large turbine/utility grid WECS, based upon the combined tower and rotor blade length, shall be 500 feet. The planning commission may waive this height requirement where this would not negatively impact adjoining properties.
The maximum level of noise permitted to be generated by any WECS shall be 50 decibels, as measured on the dBA scale, measured at the property line nearest the WECS.

Wind energy conversion systems (WECS) are prohibited in all zoning districts. There is no conditional language or exceptions provided for this prohibition, and no expiration date or time limit is specified for the ban.

All photovoltaic solar panels and support structures located in a solar energy farm shall be restricted to a maximum height of sixteen (16) feet when orientated at maximum tilt. This applies to utility-scale solar energy systems defined as solar energy farms. The unit of measurement is feet.

Section B.6 states: 'No solar energy farm shall exceed sixty (60) decibels as measured at the property line.' This is the explicit maximum noise level allowed for utility-scale solar energy systems defined as solar energy farms. The unit is assumed to be dBA, the standard unit for noise levels.

All photovoltaic solar panels and support structures associated with such facilities (excluding perimeter fencing) shall be set back a minimum of fifty (50) feet from all property lines. If the right-of-way exists as an easement, the fifty (50) foot setback shall be measured from the edge of the easement. Solar panels shall be kept at least two hundred (200) feet from an existing residential dwelling, measured to the nearest point on the residential structure. Any additional setback requirements in this Ordinance that exceed this requirement shall be adhered to.

Solar panels shall be kept at least two hundred (200) feet from an existing residential dwelling, measured to the nearest point on the residential structure. This setback applies to photovoltaic solar panels and support structures associated with solar energy farm facilities. Additionally, there is a fifty (50) foot setback from all property lines, but the 200-foot setback from residences is the relevant requirement for occupied dwellings. No multiplier based on structure height is mentioned.

No Commercial/Utility WECS shall exceed 50 dBA at the nearest structure or use. This is a clear and specific maximum noise level requirement for Commercial WECS within the jurisdiction of the City of Kimball.

Commercial/Utility WECS must be set back from property lines by one times the total height. The total height is defined as the highest point, above ground level, reached by a rotor tip or any other part of the Wind Energy Conversion System.

The setback from neighboring dwelling units for Commercial/Utility WECS is 750 feet (reciprocal for dwellings). For other structures, the setback is the greater of the fall zone (equivalent to one times total height) plus 10 feet or one times the total height. 'Total height' is defined as the highest point above ground level reached by a rotor tip or any other part of the Wind Energy Conversion System.

section: Section 16B.05 — Utility-Scale Solar Energy Collector Systems
nrel_summary: The maximum height of the system shall be twenty (20) feet, measured from the natural grade below the unit to the highest point at full tilt. This applies specifically to utility-scale solar energy collector systems as defined in the Utility-Scale Solar Energy Collector Systems Overlay District. Other height limits mentioned in the text apply only to small-scale or accessory solar energy systems, such as a maximum height of six (6) feet for residential ground-mounted systems and sixteen (16) feet for agricultural, commercial, and industrial ground-mounted systems, but these do not apply to utility-scale systems.

section: Section 16B.05 — Utility-Scale Solar Energy Collector Systems
nrel_summary: Section 16B.05.D states: 'Noise emanating from the solar energy collector system shall not exceed sixty (60) decibels (dBA) as measured from any lot line of the lot on which the system is located.' This applies specifically to utility-scale solar energy collector systems. No other maximum noise levels for utility-scale systems are provided in the text.

section: Section 16B.05 — Utility-Scale Solar Energy Collector Systems
nrel_summary: The minimum setback for all yards shall be one hundred (100) feet; however, as a condition of approval, the Township may require increased setbacks if it is determined that greater separation is necessary to adequately protect adjacent residents and property owners.

section: Section 16B.05 — Utility-Scale Solar Energy Collector Systems
nrel_summary: The minimum setback for all yards shall be one hundred (100) feet; however, as a condition of approval, the Township may require increased setbacks if it is determined that greater separation is necessary to adequately protect adjacent residents and property owners.

Dallas Township hereby temporarily prohibits the receipt of applications and issuance of all permits, licenses, and approvals for the construction or establishment of Commercial Solar Energy Systems pending further study, revisions, enactment, and effect of revised Dallas Township Zoning Ordinance regulations addressing the same. Applications, Permits, licenses, and approvals for the construction or establishment of Non-Commercial Solar Energy Systems may be processed and issued consistent with the Dallas Township Zoning Ordinance. The moratorium is effective immediately after publication on January 10, 2022, and does not have a specified expiration date, only that it continues pending further study and zoning ordinance revisions.

Wind energy system shall have a set back from all existing property lines, easements, or structures of one (1) foot of setback for each foot of total height (the vertical distance from ground to tip of blade when tip is at its highest point) or an engineer’s design of fall zone with licensed structural engineer’s stamp on design.

Wind energy system shall have a set back from all existing ... structures of one (1) foot of setback for each foot of total height (the vertical distance from ground to tip of blade when tip is at its highest point) or an engineer’s design of fall zone with licensed structural engineer’s stamp on design.

section: Sec. 305-8 Specific Requirements for Intermediate and Large Scale SES
nrel_summary: The SES shall be located no closer than the lesser of (a) fifteen (15) feet from any property line or easement or (b) the setback standards for the underlying zoning district, if any. Other setback options include twenty (20) feet from any public right-of-way or the underlying zoning district standards, and setbacks from residential dwelling units (50 feet for intermediate scale and 100 feet for large scale SES), but these do not pertain to property lines or parcels.

section: Sec. 305-8 Specific Requirements for Intermediate and Large Scale SES
nrel_summary: The SES shall be located no closer than 100 feet from any residential dwelling unit for large scale SES. Other setback options include 50 feet for intermediate scale SES from residential dwelling units, and setbacks from property lines or easements (lesser of 15 feet or underlying zoning district standards), and from public right-of-way (lesser of 20 feet or underlying zoning district standards).

Commercial WECS projects shall not exceed 175' in height and must provide proof of compliance with all FAA regulations. The height is measured from the base of the structure to the highest reach of its blade.

The noise level measured at the property line of the property on which any WECS project has been installed shall not exceed 55 decibels (dBA). This applies to all WECS projects, including commercial WECS.

All WECS projects must be setback from the property lines at a distance equal to or greater than 150 percent of the height of the structure, measured from the base of the structure to the highest reach of its blade.

Wind turbine systems must not exceed 475 feet (145 meters) in height including the rotor system. This applies to wind turbines typically rated at 1.0 megawatts or higher used in Wind Turbine Farms, which are large scale collections of commercial scale WECS used to generate utility scale electrical energy.

section: 305.53 SMALL WIND ENERGY SYSTEMS (SWES) and COMMERCIAL/ INDUSTRIAL WIND ENERGY SYSTEMS (CIWES)
nrel_summary: The maximum height of a Commercial/Industrial Wind Energy System (CIWES) shall be no taller than 160 feet in height, as explicitly stated in Section 305.53(a): 'The maximum height of a SWES or CIWES shall be no taller than 160 feet in height.' The unit 'feet' is used consistently throughout the ordinance for height measurements.

section: 305.53 SMALL WIND ENERGY SYSTEMS (SWES) and COMMERICAL/ INDUSTRIAL WIND ENERGY SYSTEMS (CIWES)
nrel_summary: The minimum setback for a Commercial/Industrial Wind Energy System (CIWES) shall be 1.1 times the total height from the nearest property line. The total height shall include the height of any structure that a tower or pole is mounted on if it is not mounted directly at ground level. The setback distance shall be measured from the center of the wind turbine base to the nearest point on the foundation of the occupied building.

section: 305.53 SMALL WIND ENERGY SYSTEMS (SWES) and COMMERICAL/ INDUSTRIAL WIND ENERGY SYSTEMS (CIWES)
nrel_summary: The minimum setback for a Commercial/Industrial Wind Energy System (CIWES) shall be 1.1 times the total height from the nearest occupied building. The total height includes the height of any structure that a tower or pole is mounted on if it is not mounted directly at ground level. The setback distance shall be measured from the center of the wind turbine base to the nearest point on the foundation of the occupied building.
Audible sound from a Wind Energy Facility shall not exceed 55 dBA, as measured at the exterior of any occupied Building on a nonparticipating landowner's Property.

All Wind Turbines shall be set back from the nearest Lot Line a distance of not less than the greater of the maximum setback requirements for that zoning classification where the turbine is located or 1.1 times the turbine height, whichever is greater. The Setback distance shall be measured to the center of the Wind Turbine base.

Wind Turbines shall be set back from the nearest occupied Building a distance not less than the greater of the maximum Setback requirements for that zoning classification where the turbine is located or 1.1 times the turbine height, whichever is greater. The Setback distance shall be measured from the center of the Wind Turbine base to the nearest point on the foundation of the occupied Building. For occupied Buildings on a nonparticipating landowner's Property, the setback is not less than five times the hub height, measured from the center of the Wind Turbine base to the nearest point on the foundation of the occupied Building.

section: § 194-59 Solar collectors and installations for major systems or solar farms

section: § 194-59 Solar collectors and installations for major systems or solar farms
nrel_summary: The Town has determined to limit the total cumulative installed capacity of major solar systems or farms within the Town to 16 MW. All projects will be on a first come basis and will be processed once a complete application has been submitted to the Town with no preference given to any one location, property owner, or developer. This limit applies specifically to major solar collection systems or solar farms, which are defined as systems principally used to capture solar energy and convert it to electrical energy to transfer to the public electric grid in order to sell electricity to or receive a credit from a public utility entity.
